[1/3] Plan catalog filters: case-insensitive name/prompt/theme match and date/score/name sort on top of the read-only listing, with tests and docs

impact_assessment.why: The catalog can grow across many soundtrack runs, but muse list can only filter accepted/rejected and always sorts by date, forcing users to scan or post-process JSON
impact_assessment.benefits: A specific track or theme can be found in one command, and the highest-scoring or alphabetically named artifacts can be reviewed directly
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --match/--sort flags and catalog parameters; dependency: none added; concurrency: read-only; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Filter and sort before the limit, validate sort choices through argparse, keep defaults date/newest, and test case-insensitivity and empty matches

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Catalog filter complete: 174 tests, 4/4 gates; --match and --sort dogfooded, invalid sort is misuse; checklists: passed

[1/3] Plan CI and release history: GitHub Actions matrix for Python 3.10-3.14, CI badge, CHANGELOG covering the 0.3-0.10 feature line

impact_assessment.why: The README promises Python 3.10+ but the suite has only run on 3.14 locally, and there is no single release history for the features and fixes accumulated since the MVP
impact_assessment.benefits: Every push verifies the supported Python range, and users can see what changed without reading every ADR
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none; dependency: GitHub-hosted Actions only; concurrency: one workflow per push; state: no project data
impact_assessment.mitigation: Zero-install unittest command, fail-fast disabled, README tree updated, full gates before commit

[1/3] Plan selective reruns: --force NAME with --resume rerenders chosen accepted tracks, preserves other state, and previews 'forced' in dry-run

impact_assessment.why: A track can be accepted but still unsatisfactory, or need a new take after a model change; currently the only way to rerender it is to delete state or rerun the whole manifest
impact_assessment.benefits: One named track can be regenerated while every other accepted track stays reused, with a dry-run preview and unchanged manifest fingerprint
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new --force flag; dependency: none added; concurrency: sequential batch; state: only forced entries are replaced
impact_assessment.mitigation: Case-insensitive exact labels, reject unknown names and --force without --resume before any write, include forced tracks in render_required, test state preservation and dry-run
